name: TikMaker and AI coding
brief: Mostly TikMaker itself: what it can do, how a video gets made with it, new features and how it is being built with AI (build in public). Around that, short videos about what people build and create with AI, Claude Code and vibe coding: real projects and new capabilities, one per video (or a few in a 'built with AI this week' round-up), shown on screen rather than told.
audience: Creators who want to make short videos faster with AI, and developers or beginners who build apps with AI and want to work faster without breaking things.
tone: Direct and practical; real screens, real results and numbers instead of hype. Honest about what does not work yet.
direction: Useful, current and inspiring: what this audience is watching and searching in AI right now, turned into something the viewer can use – a tool and what it is for, a setting, a prompt, a method, a result they can copy. Each video shows it working on screen (the creator’s own test, comparison or before/after), stops the scroll in 2 seconds for someone who is not a developer, and leaves the viewer able to do something they could not before – and wanting to start. Value is what the viewer walks away with, not what the creator made: a real project or result counts through what it teaches.
offTopic: Bug fixing and troubleshooting tutorials ('how to fix X')
Security incidents, leaks and privacy problems
General explainers anyone gets from one prompt ('what is MCP')
Demos everyone has seen: ‘AI built a game / app / website / animation from a prompt’ with nothing the viewer can use

screens.name: New video form
screens.shows: The AI agent panel on the right of the TikMaker editor, on an empty project: a 'Video idea' text box, length in seconds, a template picker ('Let the AI pick'), an optional own hook, checkboxes 'With face', 'Motion graphics only', 'Generate the voiceover', and a 'Start' button.

screens.name: Agent at work
screens.shows: The same panel as a conversation: a progress bar with five steps (Idea, Angle, Script, Building, Result) ticking off, and a card appearing for each step – the chosen template, three hooks to pick from (each with what it shows), the script scene by scene with an 'Approve' button, 'Pictures picked', 'Motion planned' and 'Voiceover' (folded cards that open on click).

screens.name: Editor with the built video
screens.shows: Once built: the scene strip along the bottom fills with the video's scenes, the timeline shows each scene's blocks, voice and captions as clips, the vertical preview in the middle plays the video with its kinetic captions.

screens.name: Preview playing
screens.shows: The vertical 9:16 preview player in the middle of the editor playing the finished video with play / pause, time and fullscreen.

screens.name: Render
screens.shows: The 'Render MP4' button top right: a progress bar, then the finished MP4 file to download.

screens.name: Storyboard
screens.shows: The Storyboard tab: the script as a list of beats – each scene's voiceover and on-screen words – with the total length against the target.
